text: The Dun Cow was a British and Welsh folkloric figure. Wales knew her as Y Fuwch Frech, the freckled cow, and Y Fuwch Laethwen Lefrith, the milk-white milch cow. Like the Glas Gaibhleann of Ireland, she gave milk to anyone who asked. Evildoers killed her for stew or milked her into a sieve. She died in Lancashire at a farm called The Old Rib, where her whale-sized rib bone was displayed. She bore two long-horned oxen, the Ychen Bannog, who killed the monstrous Afanc. Another Dun Cow belonged to an Irish saint. Her hide became vellum, made into the Book of the Dun Cow. That book records the Tain Bo Cuailnge. Koch knows it as Lebor na hUidre.
